Fee-simple lots

items.t: City lots are read parcel by parcel under Bylaw No. 3300 and the OCP (adopted November 22, 2021).

Added-unit potential is the City land story: RS1/RS2 lots permit 4 units, and 6 units if within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, under Bylaw No. 3284 (adopted June 17, 2024) — added units on an existing lot, not new lots by subdivision.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Langley City

items.t: Zoning — City of Langley Zoning Bylaw, 2025, No. 3300: Bylaw No. 3300 repeals Zoning Bylaw 1996 No. 2100 (cited at s.1.1 of the new bylaw).

Secondary suites (Bylaw No. 3300): a suite must not exceed the lesser of 100 m² and 40% of the gross floor area of the building (s.1.3 / s.2.4(c)); the registered owner must reside on the lot; at least one off-street parking space is required in addition to the two normally required for a single detached use; and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry. Garden suites and carriage homes (s.2.4(d)) are permitted in the R1 zone, with a maximum gross ground floor area of 100 m², a maximum total floor area of accessory buildings on an R1 lot of 60 m², and the registered owner residing on the lot.

ALR block (for completeness — no City ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified; principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

Bare-land strata block: Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for 5+ lots since Jul 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since Nov 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since Nov 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw. If Longlea Estates is bought as strata, these strata rules apply to it.

What a duplex looks like in Langley City

items.t: The usual duplex form: A half duplex exists only where the parcel was strata-divided into a 2-lot plan or subdivided fee-simple.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Langley City

items.t: City — zoning: City of Langley Zoning Bylaw, 2025, No. 3300 repeals Zoning Bylaw 1996 No. 2100 (cited at s.1.1 of the new bylaw). The Township of Langley's zoning frame does not govern any City property.

City — OCP and SSMUH: The City's Official Community Plan was adopted on November 22, 2021, built on the "Nexus of Community" vision adopted July 23, 2018. SSMUH: The City amended its Zoning Bylaw to permit small-scale multi-unit housing on RS1 and RS2 lots by Bylaw No. 3284, adopted June 17, 2024 (City-only) — RS1/RS2 permit 4 units, and 6 units if within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. Duplexes are the baseline form inside that framework: A two-unit building sits below the 4-unit permission.

Under Zoning Bylaw 2025 No. 3300: A secondary suite must not exceed the lesser of 100 m² and 40% of the gross floor area of the building (s.1.3 / s.2.4(c)); the registered owner must reside on the lot (s.2.4(c)(i) owner-occupancy); a suite must provide at least one off-street parking space in addition to the two normally required for a single detached use, and must be inspected, approved through a building permit and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry. A listing's "suite" claim is a claim to verify against this rule.

blocks.text: Langley City Land Use Plans: streets and boundaries

items.t: The City of Langley is a separate municipality from the Township of Langley, with its own council, Official Community Plan (OCP) and zoning bylaw — a Township rule never governs a City lot.
Fraser Highway runs through the City as its main east–west corridor, and the future SkyTrain terminus is planned at 203 Street in Langley City Centre.

blocks.text: Langley City Land Use Plans: the housing stock

items.t: The City's own growth model is attached-led: its plan documents concentrate higher density near downtown and the future station, with plex homes in the low-density neighbourhoods.

blocks.text: Langley City Land Use Plans: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The OCP is Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 3200, given final adoption on November 22, 2021, and built on the Nexus of Community vision adopted July 23, 2018 for the next 25-plus years.
A new Zoning Bylaw No. 3300 replaces Zoning Bylaw No. 2100, adopted in 1996; the City's OCP page states the new bylaw was adopted in March 2026.

OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 3319 was brought forward with Bylaw No. 3300 to keep the OCP consistent with the zoning bylaw, align Transit-Oriented Areas (TOAs) around SkyTrain stations, and add the Townhomes and Plexhome Best Practices Guide to the Development Permit Area guidelines.
Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH): Bylaw No. 3284, adopted June 17, 2024, permits 4 units on RS1 and RS2 lots, and 6 units within 400 metres of a frequent bus stop.

Secondary suites under Bylaw No. 3300: a suite may not exceed the lesser of 100 square metres and 40 percent of the building's gross floor area, the registered owner must live on the lot, one extra off-street parking space is required, and the suite must be permitted, inspected and entered in the City's secondary suites registry.

Garden suites and carriage homes in the R1 zone under Bylaw No. 3300 are capped at 100 square metres of ground floor area, with total accessory building floor area on an R1 lot capped at 60 square metres and owner occupancy required.

blocks.text: Langley City Land Use Plans: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The vision behind the plan has a name and a date: Nexus of Community, adopted July 23, 2018, is the document the 2021 OCP implements.
The OCP carries two appendices a buyer may meet in a disclosure: Appendix A, the Nicomekl River District Neighbourhood Plan, and Appendix B, District Policies.
Provincial Transit-Oriented Area rules limit the City's ability to set minimum residential parking in areas covered by the station-area tiers, which is why parking counts differ by block.
Langley Memorial Hospital at 22051 Fraser Highway serves both Langleys but sits in the Township, outside the City boundary.
Credit-card payment of City property taxes carries a 2.2 percent processing fee on the City's payment page.

blocks.text: Langley City Land Use Plans: development and new projects

items.t: Official Community Plan Amendment Bylaw No. 3319 and Zoning Bylaw No. 3300, City-wide, City of Langley: status — public hearing held November 17, 2025; the City's OCP page states Bylaw No. 3300 was adopted in March 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).

Surrey Langley SkyTrain, King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City: 16 kilometres, eight stations, three transit exchanges including Langley City Centre, budget $5.996 billion. Status: under construction, anticipated in-service date late 2029 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Langley City Land Use Plans: costs and taxes

items.t: The City's total residential tax rate for 2026 is $4.2067 per $1,000 of taxable value, of which the City general rate is $2.5937 per $1,000, with school, TransLink, Metro Vancouver and other levies making up the rest.

City water charges in the 2026 rate sheet combine a $75.00 annual flat fee with consumption charged per cubic metre; sewer and solid waste are billed under the same City utility structure — see the rate sheet for the current figures.
Whether the Speculation and Vacancy Tax applies is set by the Province's taxable-area list; Langley City buyers should confirm the property's status on the provincial page for the declaration year.

blocks.text: Langley City Land Use Plans: getting around

items.t: There is no SkyTrain station in the City today; the Surrey Langley SkyTrain project extends the Expo Line 16 kilometres on an elevated guideway from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City.
The extension includes eight stations and three transit exchanges, at Bakerview–166 Street, Willowbrook and Langley City Centre.
The City's own vision page states SkyTrain is coming to Langley City by the end of 2029 — the project page's current wording is late 2029.

blocks.text: Langley City Land Use Plans: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the lot against both documents: the OCP designation in Bylaw No. 3200 and the zone in Bylaw No. 3300, because the November 2025 amendment package changed land use on some parcels for Transit-Oriented Area consistency.
The Nicomekl River District is a named plan area inside the OCP (Appendix A), so river-adjacent lots carry a second layer of policy beyond the base zone.
